title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 83 (Satisfaction entry without company intimation)

content.overview: On evidence satisfactory to the Registrar, section 83 permits the Registrar to record full or partial satisfaction of a registered charge, or release of part of charged property/undertaking, even without company intimation. The Registrar must inform affected parties within thirty days after making the entry.
content.glance: On evidence satisfactory to the Registrar, section 83 permits the Registrar to record full or partial satisfaction of a registered charge, or release of part of charged property/undertaking, even without company intimation. The Registrar must inform affected parties within thirty days after making the entry.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 83 (Power of Registrar to make entries of satisfaction and release in absence of intimation from company). On evidence satisfactory to the Registrar concerning a registered charge, the Registrar may enter a memorandum that the debt has been paid or satisfied in whole or in part, or that part of the charged property or undertaking has been released from the charge or has ceased to form part of the company's property or undertaking. This power may be exercised notwithstanding that no intimation has been received from the company. The Registrar must inform the affected parties within thirty days after making the entry. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Evidence and Registrar power
sections.body: On evidence satisfactory to the Registrar that the debt for a registered charge has been paid or satisfied in whole or in part, the Registrar may enter a memorandum of satisfaction in whole or in part, even without company intimation.

sections.heading: Release of property
sections.body: If evidence satisfies the Registrar that part of the charged property or undertaking has been released from the charge or has ceased to form part of the company's property or undertaking, the Registrar may record that fact in the register of charges.

sections.heading: Notice to affected parties
sections.body: The Registrar must inform the affected parties within thirty days after making the entry in the register of charges.

examples.body: The Registrar may enter a memorandum of satisfaction or release where evidence shows the debt has been paid or the property released, even without an intimation from the company.

hypotheticals.question: A company does not notify the Registrar that a registered charge has been paid, but the Registrar receives satisfactory evidence of payment. What may the Registrar do under section 83?
hypotheticals.analysis: The Registrar may enter a memorandum of satisfaction in whole or in part despite the lack of company intimation, if the evidence is satisfactory. The Registrar must inform affected parties within thirty days after making the entry.

hypotheticals.question: Only part of the property subject to a registered charge has been released. Can section 83 record that partial release?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 83 expressly covers release of part of the charged property or undertaking, or property that has ceased to form part of the company's property or undertaking, when supported by evidence satisfactory to the Registrar.

distinctions.title: Company intimation and Registrar-initiated satisfaction entry
distinctions.left: Section 82 ordinarily requires the company to intimate payment or satisfaction of a charge.
distinctions.right: Section 83 allows the Registrar to record satisfaction/release on satisfactory evidence even without company intimation.

rows.right: Full/partial satisfaction or release of charged property

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the Registrar can act only after receiving company intimation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 83 expressly permits an entry notwithstanding that no intimation has been received from the company.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the provision as limited to full payment of the entire secured debt.
misconceptions.correction: The section includes payment or satisfaction in whole or in part and partial release of charged property.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the Registrar's thirty-day duty to inform affected parties.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (2) requires the Registrar to inform affected parties within thirty days after making the entry.
